author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Republican Gov. Kelly Ayotte and Democrat Cinde Warmington won their parties’ New Hampshire gubernatorial primaries Tuesday, setting the matchup for November.

Citizens Count’s election results page listed both candidates as winners Tuesday evening. Ayotte entered the election seeking a second two-year term, while Warmington, a former member of the Executive Council, is making another run for governor after competing in the 2024 Democratic primary.

The results move the contest from intraparty campaigning to a general election likely to focus on housing costs, public education, energy prices, abortion policy and management of the state budget. Ayotte will run on her first term in office, while Warmington will argue for a change in direction after years of Republican control of the corner office.

Results posted on election night are preliminary until local returns are reviewed and the state completes its canvass. The nominations nevertheless clarify the top of New Hampshire’s state ballot and give both campaigns less than two months to consolidate supporters and reach independent voters.
dek: The incumbent Republican governor and former Democratic Executive Councilor advance to the November general election.
headline: Ayotte and Warmington win New Hampshire governor primaries
